topic_candidates.brief: Test the viral claim that people can use Claude at enormous free-token volumes, then explain what “tokens” actually measure. The video separates three things viewers often confuse: the amount of text a model can read in one conversation, the number of messages an account can send over time, and the compute cost behind each request. It ends with practical ways to stretch a free allowance without presenting a paid product as the answer.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Anthropic’s current help documentation says the free plan has limited usage, while usage limits vary with message length, conversation length, model choice, tools and effort level. It also distinguishes usage limits from context or length limits, meaning a large context window is not unlimited free usage. The breakout’s 7.4-billion-token claim should therefore be treated as a testable creator claim, not as an official entitlement. topic_candidates.query: REA Reverse Engineer Anything GitHub MCP Claude Code how it works
topic_candidates.brief: Show how an AI coding agent can investigate software it cannot see the source code for. The story follows the evidence chain: observe the program, inspect binaries or runtime behavior, form a hypothesis, test it, then write an original implementation. The important correction is that REA does not magically recover the original source code; it connects an agent to reverse-engineering tools and helps the agent reason through evidence.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: The project’s GitHub documentation describes REA as an MCP server for reverse engineering across binaries, applications and runtime behavior. It says the system can inspect an app without source code, explain how a feature works, show evidence and help build an adapted version. That supports a demonstration-led explanation, while avoiding the unsupported claim that it can perfectly clone every application. ([github.com](https://github.com/BentBrains/ReverseEngineerAnything?utm_source=openai))

topic_candidates.query: open source AI motion graphics GitHub code to video agent renders MP4
topic_candidates.brief: Explain why a coding agent can make more controllable motion graphics when it is given reusable repositories instead of a blank prompt. Walk through the pipeline from plain-language brief to HTML or JavaScript scene, preview, automated visual checks and rendered video. The viewer learns why code-based animation is easier to revise than a one-shot generated clip, while also seeing the limits: timing, typography and visual QA still need human review.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: An open-source code-to-video project describes a workflow in which an AI agent writes HTML and CSS, previews its own frames, fixes problems and renders an MP4. Its documentation also emphasizes deterministic rendering, meaning the same input can reproduce the same frames. That provides a concrete engineering basis for explaining why repositories, templates and rendering tools can improve AI motion graphics.
